div.head: VI Atr Lat 32.3
div.ab: K. Arcium muri, urbes, oppida, castella, ciuitates, pontes reparentur, restaurentur, renouentur, uallis et fossis muniantur et circumuallentur.
div.note: Latin paraphrase of VI Atr (early 11th c.; K = Cotton Claudius A III f. 30, perhaps by Archbishop Wulfstan), text in column K (Liebermann’s text; until October 2026 in column T). Liebermann gives no German translation for it: for the meaning see the matching Old English chapter of VI Atr above, which it paraphrases (Liebermann prints in small type the words that correspond exactly to the Old English).; T: corrected against Gesetze I, October 2026 (was “(Liebermann’s Latin Paraphrase)”, now “∅ (moved to K)”)

note.seg: Bei Vorwiegen von Wall und Graben (s. Gl Burg 2. 5) kamen doch auch muri laut Paraphrase vor
Although rampart and ditch predominated (see Gl Burg 2. 5), muri also occurred, according to the paraphrase
An der Flotte nimmt entweder das authentische Gesetz oder die Bearbeitung, auch laut 33f., besonderen Anteil, nur im ersteren Falle vielleicht in Zusammenhang mit der Rüstung von 1008; s. o. Einl. 4
Either the authentic law or the revision takes a special interest in the fleet, as 33f. also shows; only in the former case perhaps in connection with the armament of 1008; see above Introduction 4
